clue.text: Inefficient delivery of what's native to these shores — shingle?

definitions.text: Inefficient delivery of what's native to these shores

parts.note: the letters of shingle are those of the word for the native language, jumbled up: a broken version of it

explanation.surface: A beachcomber wonders whether a delivery of local pebbles has been botched.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'shingle' as the language's name with its letters broken up: the answer, read as wordplay, gives the clue word.
explanation.definitionFit: Halting, mangled speech in the local tongue of Britain is what people call a poor command of it.

clue.text: Pioneer Running Bear was familiar with terrain

indicators.note: running here means set loose, so the letters that follow are shuffled

parts.note: to have been familiar with something is to have known it
terrain is the land or ground underfoot

explanation.surface: A frontier tale: a Native American called Running Bear knew the land well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Running Bear' looks like a name; 'Running' is the anagram signal working on BEAR plus KNEW.
explanation.definitionFit: To pioneer is to do something no one has done before, the idiom of breaking fresh soil.

clue.text: Willowy cider drinker, head down (in book)

definitions.note: used loosely as a noun, a willowy thing: the definition names a kind of willow

indicators.note: the head, or first letter, is moved down to the bottom of this vertical entry

parts.note: Rosie is the girl in Laurie Lee's memoir Cider with Rosie, the book the clue refers to

explanation.surface: A slim figure in a book downs cider with their head lowered.
explanation.walkthrough: '(in book)' points to Laurie Lee's Cider with Rosie, a classic English memoir of a Cotswold village childhood.
explanation.definitionFit: An osier is a willow species whose pliant shoots are used in basket-making.

clue.text: Old American hawk — now I see her flying

indicators.note: flying suggests the letters are scattered through the air and rearranged

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher spots an old American hawk in flight overhead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hawk' is not a bird here but a hard-liner in military matters.
explanation.definitionFit: A hawk is someone favouring military strength; the wartime general and later president fits as a past American one.

clue.text: Max, involved with English goy, marrying out

indicators.note: involved with suggests the names are tangled together, so all these letters are rearranged

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for English, set before the word goy

explanation.surface: Max gets involved with an English gentile, a case of marrying outside the faith.
explanation.definitionFit: The term from anthropology for the custom of taking a spouse from outside one's own group or tribe.

clue.text: USA goes mad, substantially lacking boundaries

indicators.note: mad suggests the letters have gone crazy and are rearranged

explanation.surface: America goes crazy, almost completely without limits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'substantially' is literal: a substance in this state has no fixed shape or bounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Matter in the state like vapour has no fixed volume or shape, expanding to fill any container.

clue.text: Islamic leader ruled country

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

parts.note: to have run a place is to have ruled it

explanation.surface: An Islamic leader governed a nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Islamic leader' suggests an ayatollah; it is just the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: The Islamic Republic in western Asia, once called Persia, is a nation.

clue.text: Bush went like the clappers in London Park area

indicators.note: in places the running inside the park's name

parts.note: Hyde Park is a large royal park in central London
a bell's clapper strikes it, so going like the clappers here means the bell rang

explanation.surface: Someone sprinted flat out through a London park to reach a shrub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'went like the clappers' is British slang for sped, but here bells with clappers rang; 'Bush' is a shrub, not a president.
explanation.definitionFit: A flowering shrub with big round heads of blue, pink or white blooms is a garden bush.

clue.text: Possible fruit of debate about protection surrounding queen and prince during race

indicators.note: during places the following pieces within the mixed letters
a possible race is only one arrangement of its letters, so the word race is rearranged

parts.note: on means about, as in a talk on a subject

indicators.note: surrounding puts the barrier around the royal letters

parts.note: a fence is a barrier giving protection
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the usual abbreviation for a queen

explanation.surface: A debate on security around the royal couple during a contest might bear fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possible' sits far from 'race' but is the only word that can signal its letters being rearranged, so the definition is 'fruit of debate'.
explanation.definitionFit: A pear variety shares its name with a formal meeting for discussion, so it is jokingly what a debate produces.

clue.text: Discharges new media projects

parts.note: E, for electronic, is the prefix of the new digital media, as in e-book
missions are undertakings or projects

explanation.surface: A firm releases a raft of digital media initiatives.
explanation.definitionFit: Releases of gas, fluid or fumes are what an exhaust or chimney gives off.

clue.text: Sound ensuing from car's idling speed

parts.note: Audi is a German make of car
a car idling has zero speed, and zero is O

explanation.surface: A noise comes from a car's engine ticking over.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective-turned-noun for recorded or broadcast sound, as opposed to pictures.

clue.text: South-east Asian girl

definitions.meaning: a member of a people living in Myanmar and Thailand

explanation.definitionFit: One word is both an ethnic group of Burma and Thailand and a familiar woman's name.

clue.text: A rejection from Le Monde for apparently prolific author?

parts.note: Le Monde is a French paper, so the rejection is the French for no

explanation.surface: A French newspaper turns down a writer who seems to produce endlessly.
explanation.walkthrough: Anthologies credit so many poems to the unnamed writer that this seems one very productive author.
explanation.definitionFit: The abbreviation for anonymous appears under countless works, as if one writer wrote them all.

clue.text: Adult in loudest possible fuss

indicators.note: in places the adult's letter inside the musical marking

parts.note: fff, fortississimo, is the musical marking for as loud as possible
A is the film-certificate abbreviation for adult

explanation.surface: A grown-up makes the loudest possible commotion.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for dithering or making an unnecessary to-do over something.

clue.text: Type of capital supplied by dope at minimum rate is source of growth for Jersey?

parts.note: seed capital is the money that starts up a new business
pot is slang for cannabis, also called dope
the lowest possible rate is zero, written O

explanation.surface: A business raises startup money from cannabis, at almost no interest, to grow in Jersey.
explanation.walkthrough: Jersey is a Channel Island famous for its new potatoes, Jersey Royals.
explanation.definitionFit: A tuber planted to grow a new crop is how the island's famous potato harvest starts.

clue.text: Company beset by money troubles might blame it

definitions.text: Company beset by money troubles might blame it

indicators.note: beset by means surrounded by, so the firm's letters sit inside
troubles means stirs up, so the letters of money are rearranged

explanation.surface: A firm short of cash might blame the wider state of business.
explanation.definitionFit: A struggling firm typically blames the country's overall financial state and trade conditions.

clue.text: Possession of drugs not primarily cool

indicators.note: not primarily means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: downers are sedative drugs
hip means fashionable, cool

explanation.surface: Holding narcotics is anything but cool.
explanation.definitionFit: Owning something, having title to it, is having it in one's possession.

clue.text: One displaying gamesmanship essentially hassled German

indicators.note: essentially points to the letters at the heart of the phrase, spanning both words

explanation.surface: A sharp operator at heart pestered a German.
explanation.walkthrough: Sledging is cricket slang for taunting the batsman to break their concentration.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricketer who verbally needles an opponent is practising a form of unsporting gamesmanship.

clue.text: Drink is English stimulant

parts.note: gin is a spirit drink
is shortens to 's

explanation.surface: A tipple described as an English pick-me-up.
explanation.definitionFit: The root of an Asian plant is taken as a tonic said to boost energy.

clue.text: Indian holiday tummy, perhaps? Try a different course

parts.note: Goa is a region of India, popular for holidays
a bout is an attack of illness, as of an upset stomach on holiday

explanation.surface: A traveller with a gut bug in India decides to change plans.
explanation.walkthrough: Goa is a beach-holiday state on India's west coast; the surface hints at a stomach upset like Delhi belly.
explanation.definitionFit: In sailing, the phrase means to change tack, steering onto a new heading.

clue.text: Northern guard sent back to be put in the picture again

indicators.note: sent back means the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: a warder is a prison guard

explanation.surface: A northern guard is returned to be briefed again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put in the picture' suggests briefing someone; it means drawn into a picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally sketched once more, so placed into the image a second time.

clue.text: Carb-heavy dish is too much in the middle of prom

indicators.note: in places the pieces inside the core letters
the middle of a word is its central letters

parts.note: OTT, over the top, means excessive

explanation.surface: A starchy meal is excessive at the height of a school dance.
explanation.definitionFit: An Italian rice dish cooked in stock is rich in carbohydrate.

clue.text: Not bad painter of lady's fingers

parts.note: OK means satisfactory, not bad
RA, Royal Academician, stands for a painter

explanation.surface: An artist who paints a woman's hands decently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lady's fingers' sounds like a portrait detail; it is a vegetable.
explanation.definitionFit: The green pod vegetable gumbo is also known by this name.

clue.text: I don't know how to cross mountains

definitions.meaning: what a quiz contestant says when declining to answer
a gap or route through a range

explanation.definitionFit: One word is both the quiz-show way of declining to answer and a route through high peaks.

clue.text: Striking unfashionable note

parts.note: out means no longer in fashion
re is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: An outmoded musical note still makes an impression.
explanation.definitionFit: Bizarre, eccentric and eye-catching: a French borrowing for strikingly unusual.

clue.text: Mysticism's central part in traditional Chinese society

indicators.note: in places the central letter inside the shortened word

parts.note: trad is short for traditional

indicators.note: the central part of a word is its middle letter

explanation.surface: The core of mysticism belongs to an old Chinese culture.
explanation.definitionFit: A Chinese secret society, especially a criminal gang, goes by this name.

clue.text: Mystic raising question about our identity

indicators.note: raising in a down entry means the letters read upwards

parts.note: the query 'If us?' wonders whether we are the ones meant

explanation.surface: A spiritual seeker asks who we really are.
explanation.definitionFit: A Muslim ascetic seeking union with God through contemplation is a mystic.

clue.text: Indian leader rejecting women-only sport

indicators.note: rejecting means turned back, so the letters are reversed

parts.note: a hen party is a women-only celebration
RU is Rugby Union

explanation.surface: A leader in India turns down a sport for women only.
explanation.definitionFit: India's first prime minister after independence led the country.

clue.text: There's nothing scariest rides exclude

parts.note: O is zero, nothing

indicators.note: rides suggests the letters are tossed about as on a funfair ride

explanation.surface: No funfair thrill is too frightening.
explanation.definitionFit: To shut someone out of a group or society, refusing to include them.

clue.text: Procedural motions could be explosive option for reds

indicators.note: explosive suggests the letters are blown apart and rearranged

explanation.surface: A violent choice for left-wing revolutionaries.
explanation.definitionFit: Objections in a meeting that the rules of debate are being broken.
